purpose: A direct-mapped cache between a host bus port and a memory bus port. Each line has a stored tag and valid bit (tag_mem, valid_mem) and four byte-lane data arrays. A read hit is answered from the arrays (L189-192, L405). A read miss refills the whole line word by word from the bus (S_DOWNLOAD_*, L223-261). A write hit updates the line and is also sent to the bus (write-through, L193-196); a write miss goes to the bus only. Accesses at or above UC_BEGIN, AMO and debug accesses bypass the cache (L171-188). A fence clears all valid bits and is forwarded (L214-221). A refill bus error invalidates the line and returns an error (L252-258).

conceptual_assets.name: Cached memory data (data array content)
conceptual_assets.flow: cached read (hit); miss refill (download); write hit (write-through)

C.why: host_rsp_o.data <= cache_i.data is the default in every state except S_DIRECT_RSP, and cache_i.data is the array word at the current address (L288, L425-428). So array content reaches the host whether or not the line is valid. The data_memory process (L410-430) has no reset or clear branch: reset (L377) and a fence (L381) clear only valid_mem, so old contents stay readable on this path.

I.why: A write hit stores host data into the line at L194 before the bus answers the write. If the answer carries err, it is only forwarded to the host (L209) and nothing reverts or invalidates the line (compare L254-255 for refills). Later hits (L189-191) then serve data that memory refused. Any corrupted byte is likewise returned as memory content on a hit.

A.why: The arrays are read every clock with no blocking condition; delivery depends on the controller (see the controller-state asset).

U.why: Requests flagged by ctrl.buf_dir (AMO, debug, or address >= UC_BEGIN; L171-173) go to the bus at L186-188. cache_o.we stays '0' (L150) and no cmd_inv is raised (L147), so a write on this path leaves the cached copy valid and stale, and later hits return the old value until a fence. With READ_ONLY = true a write hit is acknowledged at L190-191 without being written anywhere.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Corrupting a data_mem byte, or updating memory through the bypass path or through a write the bus refuses, makes L191 acknowledge a hit whose data on L156 no longer matches memory. Sampling host_rsp_o.data (L156) without ack exposes array words of invalidated or pre-reset lines.

conceptual_assets.name: Line identity (tag and valid bits) and the hit decision

C.why: A hit is acknowledged from S_LOOKUP (L189-192). A miss first runs S_DOWNLOAD_REQ/RSP once per word (L199-200, L223-250). Response latency therefore reveals which lines are resident, which is the access history of whoever shares the cache. The hit path reads neither host_req_i.priv nor host_req_i.src.

I.why: hit_o = valid_mem_rd and (tag_mem_rd = acc_tag). A set valid bit or a wrong tag turns a miss into a hit, and L191/L156 then return another address's data. cmd_new sets the valid bit and the tag at the first word request (L226 -> L385, L398), so the line counts as valid before its data arrives. Its correctness then rests on the refill finishing (ctrl.ofs, L245) or on the error invalidation (L255 -> L383).

A.why: A fence clears every valid bit (L381), which forces misses. That delays responses but does not block them.

U.why: The hit decision uses only the valid bit and the tag (L405), and the hit ack checks only rw and READ_ONLY (L190-191). host_req_i.priv is never read (only forwarded on bus_req_o at L159). So a line filled by one requester's refill is returned to any later requester, and a permission check applied to the refill downstream is not repeated on hits.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Setting a valid bit or tag through new_i, or by corruption, makes L405 raise hit_o for an address never fetched, so L191 acknowledges and L156 delivers another line's data. The latency difference between L189 and L199 tells an observer which lines another requester touched.

conceptual_assets.name: Cache controller state (FSM)

C.why: The state encodes the operation in progress, not data.

I.why: ctrl.state selects every controller output. A jump from S_DOWNLOAD_RSP to S_LOOKUP skips the error check at L254-257 and leaves an erroneous or partly filled line valid (set at L385). An unintended entry into S_CLEAR (L214-221) flushes the cache. Only unreachable encodings are caught (L263-265).

A.why: S_DIRECT_RSP (L210) and S_DOWNLOAD_RSP (L243) are left only on bus_rsp_i.ack = '1'. There is no timeout or abort, so a bus that never acknowledges keeps host_rsp_o.ack low forever (acks come only from L191, L209 and L256).

U.why: No mode overrides the sequence; the others branch only returns to S_IDLE.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Withholding bus_rsp_i.ack holds ctrl.state in S_DOWNLOAD_RSP or S_DIRECT_RSP (L243, L210), so the host is never acknowledged. Corrupting ctrl.state can bypass the error check at L254.

conceptual_assets.name: Flush (fence) request and its execution

C.why: The fence is the only operation that removes resident lines (L168-169 -> L219 -> L381). It is therefore the means to stop one requester observing or reusing another's lines.

I.why: A fence must reach S_CLEAR, where cmd_clr (L219) clears all valid bits and bus_req_o.fence (L217) goes downstream. If the pending fence in ctrl.buf_sync is lost, lines that are stale (memory changed through the bypass path, by another master, or by a refused write) keep being served by L189-191.

A.why: A fence takes priority over a request (L168 before L170) and completes in one state (L214-221); it delays but does not block.

U.why: The flush clears only valid_mem. tag_mem (L394-402) and the data arrays (L410-430) keep the flushed content, and L156 still drives array words to the host. With READ_ONLY = true the fence is not forwarded downstream (L216-217).

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Suppressing ctrl.buf_sync or cache_o.cmd_clr keeps every valid bit after a fence, so L189-191 serve lines that should have been discarded. Even when the flush works, L381 leaves the array bytes that L156 still drives.

conceptual_assets.name: Refill error status

C.why: A refill whose response carries err (possibly a denied access) is still written into the line (L236-237), and the line was already marked valid (L226 -> L385). Only the invalidation at L255 (-> inv_i, L383) keeps the next lookup from serving it.

I.why: If ctrl.buf_err is lost between L242 and L254, S_DOWNLOAD_DONE goes back to S_LOOKUP (L260). The line stays valid and the host gets a normal ack (L191) with the bad data instead of err (L257).

A.why: An error still completes the request with ack and err (L256-257).

U.why: Errors on write-through or bypass responses in S_DIRECT_RSP are forwarded to the host (L209) but never reach buf_err (bus_rsp_i.err is read only at L242). So a write hit that the bus refused leaves the updated line (L194) valid: error handling covers refills only.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Clearing ctrl.buf_err, or blocking cmd_inv or inv_i, turns a refused refill into a valid line: L260 returns to lookup, L191 acknowledges data the bus refused, and host_rsp_o.err is never set at L257.

conceptual_assets.name: Bypass (direct access) decision

C.why: Wrongly bypassing only sends the request to the bus, which is the uncached behaviour; no value is disclosed by the decision itself.

I.why: ctrl.buf_dir decides whether the request is served from or filled into the cache (L189-205) or passed to the bus (L186-188). Forcing it to '0' caches accesses to the region >= UC_BEGIN and AMO or debug accesses: the host gets stale cached values for them (L191), and an AMO is no longer carried out by the bus.

A.why: Forcing a bypass costs latency only.

U.why: host_req_i.debug and host_req_i.amo, attributes the requester supplies, route the access around the cache without updating or invalidating it (L186-188; defaults L147, L150). The debug or AMO view of memory therefore diverges from what the cache serves to normal requests until a fence.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Forcing ctrl.buf_dir to '0' at L186 makes an uncached-region, debug or AMO request hit the cache (L191) or refill a line (L200) instead of reaching the bus. A debug or AMO write that bypasses at L187 leaves a stale valid line that later hits return.

hypotheses: Timing channel on residency (CA2 C): exploiting the hit (L189-192) versus refill (L199-250) latency needs an attacker that shares the cache with a victim and can time its requests; that sharing is outside this source.

Privilege-agnostic hits (CA2 U): L189-191 never read host_req_i.priv, which is only forwarded on bus_req_o (L159). This harms only if access checks are made downstream of the cache on the refill request rather than before the request reaches it.
Exposure without ack (CA1 C): host_rsp_o.data carries the array word of any line on every non-direct cycle (L156). This harms only if a requester can sample data while ack is '0'.
bus_req_o.lock is held at '1' for every word of a refill (L230, L240). If downstream treats it as exclusive bus ownership, a requester that forces repeated misses keeps other masters waiting.

Address stability: the hit compare (L405) matches a tag registered in the previous cycle against the current host_req_i.addr, and the error invalidation in S_DOWNLOAD_DONE uses host_req_i.addr (L149) rather than ctrl.idx. Both assume the host holds the address stable for the whole request, a bus-protocol property outside this source.
READ_ONLY = true: a write is acknowledged and dropped (L190-191, L199-200) with no error. This harms only if a writer is attached to a read-only instance.
UC_BEGIN (a generic, not in the map) defines which addresses bypass the cache (L171). A wrong value makes a device region cacheable.

map_assessment.used_for: Indexing all 86 elements with their occurrences, and following direct edges. Data edges gave the data path (host_req_i.data/bus_rsp_i.data -> cache_o.data -> wdata_i -> data_mem_b0..b3 -> rdata_o -> cache_i.data -> host_rsp_o.data). Control edges gave the guards on ctrl_nxt.state and host_rsp_o.ack. Connections carried values across the sub-block boundary. Constant drivers showed when each command bit is raised. RESETS edges showed that only valid_mem and valid_mem_rd are reset in the memory block. Per-element occurrences showed that bus_rsp_i.err is read only at L242 and that host_req_i.priv has no local use.
map_assessment.insufficient_for: Storage of record fields (ctrl.* are registers through L126 but are marked storage 'none'). Whole-record assignments are not pushed down to fields (L159 drives every bus_req_o field; L209 drives host_rsp_o.data/ack/err from bus_rsp_i). Generics (UC_BEGIN at L171; READ_ONLY at L190 and L199 are not recorded; only bus_req_o.fence carries a READ_ONLY condition). Timing and order, such as the one-cycle registered tag and valid read against the live acc_tag, the cache write at L194 before the bus answer at L209, and the valid bit set at L226 before the data arrives. Absences, such as no privilege check on hits and no clear of the data arrays, which must be read from the source. The loop through external memory (bus_req_o.addr -> bus_rsp_i.data). The meaning of bus record fields such as lock, priv and debug.
map_assessment.errors_found: ctrl.state, ctrl.buf_req, ctrl.buf_sync, ctrl.buf_err, ctrl.buf_dir, ctrl.tag, ctrl.idx and ctrl.ofs have storage 'none' but are stored (ctrl <= ctrl_nxt under rising_edge, L125-126). bus_req_o.data, .ben, .src, .priv, .debug, .amo and .amoop are marked 'undriven' but are driven by L159. host_rsp_o.data's record omits its second driver, L209.
